prompt: A crashed flying saucer UFO, half-buried in its impact crater. SHAPE IS CRITICAL - the saucer is a WIDE THIN LENS, NOT a dome: total diameter 36-40 blocks, total hull thickness at most 7 blocks (width-to-height ratio at least 5:1). Build it as stacked horizontal disks: a protruding rim ring at the widest point (the classic saucer lip), a few shrinking disks above it, a shallow tapering underside below. On top dead-center: ONE small GLASS cockpit dome (radius 2-3). PALETTE: hull is STONE and COBBLE only (alternate in concentric rings for metal paneling); GLASS only for the dome and a single row of rim portholes; NO ICE, NO BRICK on the hull surface. Tilt the saucer ~10-15 degrees by shifting the disk centers sideways as they stack, with the low edge crushed into the crater floor and the high edge lifted free of the ground. DIG the crater: a wide AIR gouge below ground trailing behind the saucer, rimmed with thrown-up DIRT and STONE. A couple of fallen OAK_LOG trees at the crater rim. Keep the ground/debris understated - the saucer is the star. Ominous, heavy, instantly readable as a flying saucer. Use the full solid-block budget.
